16:1.sourceText: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ Σαδδουκαῖοι πειράζοντες ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν σημεῖον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπιδεῖξαι αὐτοῖς.
16:1.targetText: And the Pharisees and Sadducees having come, tempting, questioned Him, to show to them a sign from Heaven,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with Heaven.

16:2.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὀψίας γενομένης λέγετε Εὐδία, πυρράζει γὰρ ὁ οὐρανός·
16:2.targetText: and He answering said to them, “Evening having come, you say, Fair weather, for the sky is red,

groups.note: The actual reddening verb πυρράζει supplies the English is red predicate; no additional Greek be verb is invented.

16:3.sourceText: καὶ πρωΐ Σήμερον χειμών, πυρράζει γὰρ στυγνάζων ὁ οὐρανός. τὸ μὲν πρόσωπον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ γινώσκετε διακρίνειν, τὰ δὲ σημεῖα τῶν καιρῶν οὐ δύνασθε;
16:3.targetText: and at morning, Foul weather today, for the sky is red—gloomy; hypocrites, you indeed know to discern the face of the sky, but the signs of the times you are not able!

groups.note: The actual reddening verb πυρράζει supplies is red, while the following darkening participle supplies gloomy.
The actual darkening participle στυγνάζων is condensed into gloomy; its source verbal form is preserved.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes the hypocrites address; pinned N1904 has no corresponding hypocrites noun in this verse.

16:4.sourceText: γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς σημεῖον ἐπιζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ. καὶ καταλιπὼν αὐτοὺς ἀπῆλθεν.
16:4.targetText: An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and a sign will not be given to it, except the sign of Jonah the prophet”; and having left them He went away.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes the prophet title after Jonah; pinned N1904 has Jonah without that added title.

16:5.sourceText: Καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἰς τὸ πέραν ἐπελάθοντο ἄρτους λαβεῖν.
16:5.targetText: And His disciples having come to the other side, forgot to take loaves,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with His disciples.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly states the disciples possessor His; pinned N1904 has the disciples with no separate possessive pronoun here.

16:6.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὁρᾶτε καὶ προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.
16:6.targetText: and Jesus said to them, “Beware, and take heed of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees”;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before Jesus is not separately expressed in English.

16:7.sourceText: οἱ δὲ διελογίζοντο ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄρτους οὐκ ἐλάβομεν.
16:7.targetText: and they were reasoning in themselves, saying, “Because we took no loaves.”

16:8.sourceText: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, ὀλιγόπιστοι, ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχετε;
16:8.targetText: And Jesus having known, said to them, “Why reason you in yourselves, you of little faith, because you took no loaves?

groups.note: The actual vocative adjective ὀλιγόπιστοι addresses the little-faith people, rendered you of little faith as one adjective-based address; no separate Greek faith noun is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before Jesus is not separately expressed in English.
N1904 has ἔχετε, you have, whereas LSV follows the took wording. The Greek possession verb is not an actual taking verb and is left unpaired at this differing predicate.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV makes the saying recipients explicit; pinned N1904 has said followed directly by the question, without a separate recipient pronoun.
LSV follows the taking predicate here, whereas pinned N1904 has you have; no Greek taking verb is written at this position in the named source witness.

16:9.sourceText: οὔπω νοεῖτε, οὐδὲ μνημονεύετε τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους τῶν πεντακισχιλίων καὶ πόσους κοφίνους ἐλάβετε;
16:9.targetText: Do you not yet understand, nor remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many hand-baskets you took up?

16:10.sourceText: οὐδὲ τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους τῶν τετρακισχιλίων καὶ πόσας σπυρίδας ἐλάβετε;
16:10.targetText: Nor the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many baskets you took up?

16:11.sourceText: πῶς οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι οὐ περὶ ἄρτων εἶπον ὑμῖν; προσέχετε δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.
16:11.targetText: How do you not understand that I did not speak to you of bread—to take heed of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees?”

groups.note: N1904 has the plural imperative προσέχετε, take heed, while LSV presents the renewed warning as to take heed. The same heed-taking predicate is retained with its original imperative form.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek connective δέ introducing the warning is not separately expressed in the English dash-linked continuation.

16:12.sourceText: τότε συνῆκαν ὅτι οὐκ εἶπεν προσέχειν ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν ἄρτων, ἀλλὰ ἀπὸ τῆς διδαχῆς τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.
16:12.targetText: Then they understood that He did not say to take heed of the leaven of the bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

groups.note: The actual genitive article/bread constituent supplies of the bread as one case-governed expression.

16:13.sourceText: Ἐλθὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὰ μέρη Καισαρίας τῆς Φιλίππου ἠρώτα τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγων Τίνα λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;
16:13.targetText: And Jesus, having come to the parts of Caesarea Philippi, was asking His disciples, saying, “Who do men say I am—the Son of Man?”

groups.note: The actual infinitive εἶναι, to be, is recast as finite am in the first-person English question; it does not itself encode the separately supplied I pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with Jesus, Philippi, His disciples or men.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly makes the question first person, I am—the Son of Man. Pinned N1904 asks who people say the Son of Man to be, without a separate first-person pronoun in this question.

16:14.sourceText: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Οἱ μὲν Ἰωάνην τὸν Βαπτιστήν, ἄλλοι δὲ Ἡλείαν, ἕτεροι δὲ Ἱερεμίαν ἢ ἕνα τῶν προφητῶν.
16:14.targetText: And they said, “Some, John the Immerser, and others, Elijah, and others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.”

16:15.sourceText: λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι;
16:15.targetText: He says to them, “And you—who do you say I am?”

groups.note: The actual first-person accusative με is the subject of the Greek infinitive to be, recast as nominative I in the English finite I am question. Its original case remains accusative.

16:16.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος εἶπεν Σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος.
16:16.targetText: And Simon Peter answering said, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

16:17.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Μακάριος εἶ, Σίμων Βαριωνᾶ, ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα οὐκ ἀπεκάλυψέν σοι ἀλλ’ ὁ Πατήρ μου ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
16:17.targetText: And Jesus answering said to him, “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jona, because flesh and blood did not reveal [it] to you, but My Father who is in the heavens.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with Jesus or My Father.

unmappedTarget.reason: English explicitly supplies the revealed object it; no corresponding object pronoun is written with the Greek reveal verb here.
English supplies a copula in who is in the heavens; the Greek has an article with the locative phrase and no written be verb there.

16:18.sourceText: κἀγὼ δέ σοι λέγω ὅτι σὺ εἶ Πέτρος, καὶ ἐπὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πέτρᾳ οἰκοδομήσω μου τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, καὶ πύλαι Ἅιδου οὐ κατισχύσουσιν αὐτῆς.
16:18.targetText: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My Assembly, and [the] gates of Hades will not prevail against it;

groups.note: The actual prevailing compound κατισχύω supplies prevail against, with the genitive Assembly pronoun as its complement.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with this rock or My Assembly.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV supplies the definite article before gates; pinned N1904 writes gates without an article.

16:19.sourceText: δώσω σοι τὰς κλεῖδας τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν δήσῃς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται δεδεμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν λύσῃς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται λελυμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
16:19.targetText: and I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of the heavens, and whatever you may bind on the earth will be having been bound in the heavens, and whatever you may loose on the earth will be having been loosed in the heavens.”

groups.note: The actual perfect passive participle δεδεμένον supplies having been bound, while the separate future be verb supplies will be. The periphrastic form is grammatical information, not an added timing conclusion.
The actual perfect passive participle λελυμένον supplies having been loosed, while the separate future be verb supplies will be.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes an initial and before I will give; pinned N1904 starts directly with the giving verb.

16:20.sourceText: τότε ἐπετίμησεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ εἴπωσιν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός.
16:20.targetText: Then He charged His disciples that they may say to no one that He is Jesus the Christ.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with His disciples.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly writes the disciples possessor His; pinned N1904 has the disciples without a separate possessive pronoun here.
LSV includes Jesus in the reported identity; pinned N1904 has He is the Christ without that name in this verse.

16:21.sourceText: Ἀπὸ τότε ἤρξατο Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς δεικνύειν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀπελθεῖν καὶ πολλὰ παθεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ ἀρχιερέων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθῆναι.
16:21.targetText: From that time Jesus began to show to His disciples that it is necessary for Him to go away to Jerusalem, and to suffer many things from the elders, and chief priests, and scribes, and to be put to death, and the third day to rise.

groups.note: The actual accusative αὐτόν is the subject of the necessary infinitive construction, rendered for Him. The relation belongs to the case-governed subject, not an invented Greek for preposition.
The actual passive-form rising verb ἐγερθῆναι is rendered to rise. The original grammatical voice remains visible rather than being changed to match the English active expression.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 explicitly names Jesus Christ here; LSV has Jesus without the additional Christ title in this verse.

16:22.sourceText: καὶ προσλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ὁ Πέτρος ἤρξατο ἐπιτιμᾶν αὐτῷ λέγων Ἵλεώς σοι, Κύριε· οὐ μὴ ἔσται σοι τοῦτο.
16:22.targetText: And having taken Him aside, Peter began to rebuke Him, saying, “Be kind to Yourself, Lord; this will not be to You”;

groups.note: The actual second-person dative σοι is recast reflexively in English to Yourself in the wish; no distinct Greek reflexive pronoun is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before Peter is not separately expressed in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies Be in the adjectival wish Be kind to Yourself; the Greek has the propitious/kind adjective and dative pronoun without an explicit be verb.

16:23.sourceText: ὁ δὲ στραφεὶς εἶπεν τῷ Πέτρῳ Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου, Σατανᾶ· σκάνδαλον εἶ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι οὐ φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
16:23.targetText: and He having turned, said to Peter, “Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling-block to Me, for you do not mind the things of God, but the things of men.”

groups.note: The actual first-person genitive ἐμοῦ complements the stumbling-block expression, rendered to Me; its source case remains genitive.

16:24.sourceText: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἐλθεῖν, ἀπαρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι.
16:24.targetText: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “If anyone wills to come after Me, let him disown himself, and take up his cross, and follow Me,

groups.note: The actual θέλω verb expresses willing or wanting, not a future auxiliary.
The original third-person imperative take up continues the English let him construction from disown; its imperative person and form are retained.
The original third-person imperative follow continues the English let him construction; no separate Greek infinitive is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with Jesus or his cross.

16:25.sourceText: ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι, ἀπολέσει αὐτήν· ὃς δ’ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ, εὑρήσει αὐτήν.
16:25.targetText: for whoever may will to save his life will lose it, and whoever may lose his life for My sake will find it;

groups.note: The actual causal ἕνεκεν with the first-person genitive supplies for My sake; the relation and its personal complement remain distinct source identities.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with the English his-life phrases.

16:26.sourceText: τί γὰρ ὠφεληθήσεται ἄνθρωπος ἐὰν τὸν κόσμον ὅλον κερδήσῃ, τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ζημιωθῇ; ἢ τί δώσει ἄνθρωπος ἀντάλλαγμα τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ;
16:26.targetText: for what is a man profited if he may gain the whole world, but of his life suffer loss? Or what will a man give as an exchange for his life?

groups.note: N1904 has a future passive benefit verb ὠφεληθήσεται, will be benefited, while LSV uses the present passive question is a man profited. The actual benefit head and source future form are retained.

The actual passive loss verb ζημιωθῇ with the life object supplies suffer loss of his life; English fronts its of-life complement. The relation belongs to the loss expression, not an invented Greek preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with the English his-life expressions.

16:27.sourceText: μέλλει γὰρ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ Πατρὸς αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ, καὶ τότε ἀποδώσει ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν πρᾶξιν αὐτοῦ.
16:27.targetText: For the Son of Man is about to come in the glory of His Father, with His messengers, and then He will reward each according to his work.

16:28.sourceText: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰσίν τινες τῶν ὧδε ἑστώτων οἵτινες οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ αὐτοῦ.
16:28.targetText: Truly I say to you, there are certain of those standing here who will not taste of death until they may see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.”

groups.note: The actual genitive death noun supplies of death as the taste-verb complement; no Greek of preposition is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek quotation connector ὅτι is not separately expressed before the English declaration there are.
